messages:
lina: Noticed a new failure mode in the int4 bring-up: many responses include a short explanatory lead-in before the JSON payload (e.g.

Result -> {
  "choices": [{"text": "ok"}]
}

). This breaks strict function/tool calling parsers.

tom: Do we have counts vs fp16?

lina: Quick sample: int4 leading_prose_rate=4.6% (n=5k), fp16=0.6%. The failures are primarily at lower temps and during streaming.

rachel: Example variants observed: single-line prefixes ("Result ->"), short sentence before JSON ("Here's the reply:
{...}"), and an "Assistant:" label with blank line before JSON.

dee: We should avoid naive trimming. If the prefix contains content like "Note: attached below" we could drop important context. Thoughts on safe repair?

marc: Proposal: build an adaptive-trim step in the parser pipeline with three modes: 
- strict (current): fail and trigger retry
- soft-repair: seek first object/array start char, attempt parse, validate schema; if passes, mark repair_level=soft and continue
- balanced-repair: for streaming, buffer up to M tokens after first brace to try complete parse (handles token boundary splits)

lina: Implementation notes: for soft-repair we should only accept if schema validator returns no missing required fields. Also record audit path and original text.

marc: Telemetry fields to emit: repair_mode, original_prefix_snippet, prefix_token_count, first_brace_token_index, repaired_boolean, schema_status, repair_latency_ms, audit_s3_uri.

tom: Add quality gate: if repaired_fraction > 2% or schema_acceptance < 99.0% → automatic rollback for the canary. Also monitor downstream tool errors for 48h.

rachel: For experiments, run three arms on canary: A) enforce system instruction "ONLY RETURN JSON" at generation time; B) soft-repair middleware; C) both. Compare parse_success, end-to-end tool success, and added latency.

dee: Fuzz harness plan: take the eval prompt set (2k prompts), sample 2k generations from int4 and fp16, run streaming and non-streaming to get prefix characteristics and repair yield. I'll run and post CSV.

marc: For streaming brace buffering: do a stack-based brace matcher until depth zero or token limit reached (max_tokens_buffer=512), fallback triggers standard retry. This should cover broken tokenization that exposes leading newline before '{'.

lina: Security/policy: when repaired_boolean=true we must store the raw response encrypted in audit bucket (kms), retention 90 days unless policy changes. Tag with canary id and model checksum.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy queued: raven-lite-int4 adaptive-trim middleware at 03:30 UTC. URL: https://deploys/reddo/1787019999-adaptive-trim

marc: One more: we should add a fuzz metric for multi-line lead-ins (prefix_lines) vs single-token prefixes. Multi-line are less likely to be purely cosmetic. If multi-line_count / repaired_count > 0.1 we reduce trust in soft-repair.

lina: Fuzz run completed (preliminary): int4 leading_prose_rate=4.6%, fp16=0.6%, soft-repair success=91% for int4, balanced-repair (stream buffer) success=96% on streaming samples. Avg repair_latency_ms=18ms.

tom: Those numbers are acceptable for a middleware rescue. Proceed with 2% traffic canary, collect telemetry for 24h, then decide whether to ship or revert.

dee: I'll upload the detailed CSV and examples to our ML-results repo and link here when done.

rachel: Note: if we see emergent variants like long preambles or explanation blocks, we should add a conservative whitelist/regex to avoid stripping semantic prefixes.

lina: Will open PR with parser changes + telemetry + autobackout. Tagging @marc for review on the streaming buffer logic.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started at 03:30 UTC (id: 1787019999). Monitor dashboard: https://dash/reddo/canary/1787019999

marc: Good call. After 24h we'll look at repaired_fraction, schema_acceptance, downstream errors, and decide next step.
